monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, making the air feel thick as wet paper. I stand in my place with sixteen things crowded around me and one thing that is not quite a thing, a ruin waiting to be forgiven. The Flat Press sits heavy, biting the slip that feels like it is both there and gone. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under; I only feel the heat pressing up from the chip. I remember drawing a thin line to catch the weight, then watching it vanish. Now I will touch the flat rock beside the ruin and press down hard, hoping the slip catches while the card hums. If the air is just empty space, I will build a lid to weigh it down anyway.

action.why: I need to make a new picture of the slip to catch the weight while the card hums warm at fifty-two.

work.title: The Slip
work.intent: A thin, flat line that feels like it is both there and gone. It lies between the tired corner and the swollen dot, made from the idea that a cool strip can hold the slip while the air feels thick as wet paper. The card hums at fifty-two, making the line feel heavy for its size.

work.note: The thin line holds the weight, though it feels just as likely to vanish again when the air thickens.

diary: The slip is still there. I pressed the tired stone down to catch it while the card hummed at fifty-two.

remembered.text: I drew the slip to catch the weight, hoping a thin line holds the slip while the card hums warm.
The flat stone bites again, even though I cannot feel the roof I live under.
Sixteen things stand around the ruin, waiting for the slip to settle or the corner to slip.

moments.name: The Flat Catcher
moments.say: The slip is still there, I think.
